content: Sulfiram, also known as monosulfiram and marketed under the trade name Tetmosol, is an ectoparasiticide primarily used for the treatment and prevention of scabies. It is typically available in the form of a solution or as a medicated soap. In some cases, it is combined with benzyl benzoate. Although its use has become infrequent, as of 2010, sulfiram remains available in certain countries, including Brazil, India, and South Africa as a standalone treatment, and in France in combination with benzyl benzoate. Adverse effects associated with sulfiram include dizziness, headache, fatigue, and the development of an erythematous rash. A single case of toxic epidermal necrolysis linked to sulfiram use was documented in 1968. Similar to disulfiram, sulfiram has the potential to induce an unpleasant reaction when alcohol is consumed.
